newsitem.title: UK: London shares seen weaker after Wall Street dip.
newsitem.headline: London shares seen weaker after Wall Street dip.

text.p: UK shares are expected to open moderately lower on Wednesday as investors take a breather after pushing the FTSE 100 to new closing highs the past 11 sessions.
A weak finish on Wall Street coupled with a lacklustre bond market should be enough to encourage some light profit-taking but the market's uptrend is still on the upside, dealers said.
"This market has been quite resilient so I can't see any large sell-off on the horizon," the head of trading at a large brokerage said.
"Institutions have a lot of cash and have been buying on the dips."

U.S. blue chips closed slightly easier on Tuesday amid sagging bond prices. The Dow Industrials Average closed down 18.54 points to 7,274.21. The high-technology laden Nasdaq Composite index finished 10.60 points easier to 1,333.59.

U.S. treasuries in Tokyo were little changed from New York's closing levels, with the U.S. June T-bond down 1/32 to 109-24/32 by 0750 GMT while the yield on the benchmark 30-year long bond stood at 6.93 percent compared with 6.88 percent at this time on Tuesday.
Technical analysts said the FTSE was likely to test near-term support at 4,670-4,675 today, with a break of that range on a closing basis signalling a further decline toward 4,620.
Near-term resistance is seen at 4,720, around the FTSE's record intra-day trading high, set on Tuesday.
Cable & Wireless Plc is expected to the be the main early focus of attention after the company reported full-year pre-tax profits of 1.42 billion stg, at the top end of market expectations.
Other companies reporting results include Commercial Union Plc, with first quarter operating profits of 102 million stg and Imperial Tobacco with first-half pre-tax profits of 143 million stg.
Safeway Plc reported full-year pre-tax, pre-exceptional profits of 430 million stg and said same store sales were up 3.7 percent in the first six weeks of the current year.
Elsewhere, Centrica Plc said it had signed a deal to sell gas to Germany's Thyssengas.

UK unemployment and unit wage cost data, due at 0830 GMT was not expected to have a major impact on prices. Both bond and share markets will pay closer attention to U.S. producer price data for April, due at 1230 GMT, dealers said. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
